summary: Kengo Harimoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Nagasaki University, Kyushu University, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, 1999 under Wilhelm Halbfass). Harimoto held posts at Temple, Leiden, Groningen, Hamburg, Mahidol, and Naples "L'Orientale" universities.
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1984. Ishii held a post at Kokugakuin University from circa 1989 to 2024.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1971 to 1981 under Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1984, Matsuo held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.
Kenji Shimada was a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941. Shimada later held a post as a researcher at Kyoto University from circa 1949 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indology scholar who conducted exchange doctoral research at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop (2015–2016). Takahashi held posts at Kyoto University in 2018 and as a fellow at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jozef Deleu. Watanabe held a post at Taisho University circa 1978.

Kenjiu Kasawara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Kasawara studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and studied under Friedrich Max Müller between 1879 and 1882 as well as under Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University (~1916–1919) and under Kitarō Nishida (~1922–1925). Yanagida later held a post at Hirosaki University.
Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. Naganuma held posts at Kurume University and Kyushu University, where Naganuma was an emeritus professor circa 1946.

Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Lipman studied for a doctorate under Herbert V. Günther and held a post as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Adrian Raine Kennedy was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1949–1962). Kennedy held a post at Cornell University from circa 1964 to 2005.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned a doctorate at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe. Lee held a post at Stetson University, attested in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at UC Santa Barbara and Australian National University. Zysk held posts at Eastern Michigan University (attested 1989) and the University of Copenhagen (attested 2012–2017), among others.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the City University of New York and studied at Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, and Peking University. Guest held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara (~1908–1912). Saunders was a professor at the Pacific School of Religion and lecturer at the University of California from circa 1921 to 1935.

Kenneth K. Inada was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Inada held a professorship at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). Tanaka held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1984, 1987) and Musashino University (1998, 2003, 2008, 2014).

Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1985–1989). Valpey held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Roy Norman was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Downing College, Cambridge. Norman held posts at the University of Cambridge (1955–1992) and edited for the Pali Text Society (1981–1996).
